newsitem.title: CANADA: Tee-Comm seen restructuring in court.
newsitem.headline: Tee-Comm seen restructuring in court.

text.p: Tee-Comm Electronics Inc was seen headed for bankruptcy protection after announcing today that Bank of Montreal was reviewing its demand credit facility, analysts said on Wednesday.

"This could be entering into some kind of court-assisted restructuring before the end of the month," said analyst Philip Benson with brokerage MMI Group Inc, adding that "it could be by the end of the week."
Milton, Ontario-based Tee-Comm, a satellite television firm, declined comment.

Tee-Comm, which took on the huge U.S. direct broadcast satellite players and recently launched a Canadian service, entered the market too late and was competing against deep-pocketed players, analysts said.
"They're an ant and they're trying to run with the elephants in a stampede," said Duncan Stewart, portfolio manager at Tera Capital.
Tee-Comm's competitors include GM Hughes Electronics Corp and MCI Communications Corp.
Stewart said that since most of Tee-Comm's rivals were so big, it was unlikely that any would be interested in buying it before it restructured in court, Stewart said.
Tee-Comm said earlier today that it was negotiating with replacement financiers, a major supplier and holders of its subordinated convertible debentures to effect a restructuring.

Analyst Benson said he did not believe Tee-Comm could assemble additional financing for the cash-intensive business of satellite service. "The trough's run dry and nobody wants to step up to the plate."
Tee-Comm shares dropped 0.21 to 0.68 today on more than a million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange. It fell 3/16 to 1/2 on Nasdaq.
News of financial problems surfaced in recent weeks, driving the shares down to penny-stock level. Tee-Comm's 52-week high in Toronto was 16.10.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109 or lydia.zajc@reuters.com))
